insights.title: Three securities class actions span 2023-2025
insights.summary: Two Section 10(b)/20(a) class actions in N.D. Cal. (Hayes, and the Pension Fund Action) name the CEO and, in one case, the chief products officer. Together they cover purchasers from Feb 7, 2023 to Oct 22, 2024. A third action, Tripathi v. Enphase, was filed February 17, 2026 against the company, CEO and CFO for purchasers between April 22, 2025 and October 28, 2025. Motion-to-dismiss rulings are pending in all three.
insights.uw_relevance: These are active securities claims against the company and named senior officers. The alleged misstatement periods are not overlapping and run continuously from early 2023 to late 2025.

insights.title: Revenue down about 20% year over year
insights.summary: Revenue was $292M in FY2026 Q2, down 19.6% YoY, after $283M in FY2026 Q1, down 20.6% YoY. FY2026 Q1 posted an operating loss of $30M and a net loss of $7M. In Q2, IQ Battery MWh shipped fell 40%. US revenue fell $44.4M (16%), attributed to the Section 25D credit expiration, and international revenue fell 29%.
insights.uw_relevance: A sustained, policy-driven revenue decline puts pressure on operating results and on the company's forward-looking disclosures. Declines of this kind often feature in disclosure-based securities claims.

insights.title: Q2 profit aided by one-time tariff refunds
insights.summary: After IEEPA tariffs were invalidated, the company received refunds and interest of about $41.0M in Q2 2026 and $11.0M in July 2026. Of these, $45.4M was recorded as a reduction to Q2 cost of revenues, which supported Q2 operating income of $52M. New Section 301 tariffs of 10% to 12.5% were announced July 23, 2026, and LFP battery cells remain sole-sourced from two vendors in China.
insights.uw_relevance: Reported Q2 2026 profitability includes a non-recurring benefit, so earnings quality and disclosure of the refund's effect matter. Tariff changes and China-concentrated cell sourcing are ongoing margin and supply risks.

insights.title: Operating and free cash flow sharply lower
insights.summary: Free cash flow fell from $586M in FY2023 and $480M in FY2024 to $96M in FY2025. Operating cash flow followed the same path: $697M, $514M and then $137M. In FY2026, free cash flow was $83M in Q1 and $26M in Q2.
insights.uw_relevance: Much lower internal cash generation leaves less room to absorb litigation costs, tariff shocks or further demand weakness.

insights.title: Liquidity partly depends on tax credit sales
insights.summary: In March 2026 the company sold $235.0M of 2025 AMPTC at 93% of face value, a discount of about $16.5M plus about $2.5M in fees. In June 2026 it agreed to sell up to $150.0M of 2026 AMPTC on the same terms. Of that amount, $37.5M of Q1 2026 credits were sold for about $34.9M.
insights.uw_relevance: Section 45X credit sales are a material liquidity source. That source depends on continued FEOC and domestic content compliance under evolving Treasury guidance, which is a disclosure-sensitive area.

insights.title: Distributor and installer distress raises credit risk
insights.summary: Management states that prolonged solar demand softness has led to reduced liquidity, bankruptcies and closures among distributors and installers. A customer that filed Chapter 11 in 2024 led to a $6.2M receivable write-off in FY2025.
insights.uw_relevance: Counterparty stress in the sales channel can cause further write-offs, earnings volatility and questions about the adequacy of credit-loss reserves.

insights.title: Buybacks halted after repurchases exceeded earnings
insights.summary: Share repurchases were $410M in FY2023 and $391M in FY2024; the FY2024 amount equaled 3.81x net income. Repurchases fell to $130M in FY2025 and have been $0 in every quarter from FY2025 Q3 through FY2026 Q2.
insights.uw_relevance: The heavy FY2024 buybacks took place during class periods now in litigation, which could draw scrutiny of capital-allocation decisions. The current halt preserves cash.

followups.question: What is the current status and defense strategy for the three securities class actions: the Hayes motion-to-dismiss hearing set for September 17, 2026, the pending ruling in the Pension Fund Action after the court vacated its hearing, and the Tripathi amended complaint due September 8, 2026? Have all three been noticed to the D&O program?
followups.rationale: Three non-overlapping class periods running from February 2023 to October 2025 against the CEO, CFO and chief products officer are the most direct source of securities claim severity and defense cost.

followups.question: For the Collins v. Kothandaraman derivative suit in Delaware Chancery, which directors and executives are named, were their challenged stock sales made under Rule 10b5-1 trading plans, and has the board formed a special litigation committee or responded to any demand?
followups.rationale: Insider-sale and fiduciary-breach allegations target individual directors and officers personally, and these claims are often non-indemnifiable Side A exposures.

followups.question: How was the $45.4M IEEPA tariff refund, recorded as a reduction to Q2 2026 cost of revenues, disclosed in the earnings release and call, and how does management describe Q2 operating income of $52M and its outlook without this benefit?
followups.rationale: A non-recurring benefit that supports reported profit, during a period of active disclosure litigation, raises earnings-quality and misstatement risk.

followups.question: How did management communicate the expected impact of the Section 25D credit expiration in guidance during the April 22 to October 28, 2025 Tripathi class period? How do actual results compare: Q2 2026 revenue down 19.6% YoY, IQ Battery MWh shipped down 40%, and US revenue down $44.4M?
followups.rationale: The gap between earlier forward-looking statements and the later policy-driven revenue decline is the likely factual core of the newest securities claim.

followups.question: Who is the director appointed effective June 11, 2026 when the board expanded to eight members? What are this director's independence status, committee assignments and any role in overseeing the pending litigation?
followups.rationale: Board composition and the independence of litigation oversight affect how derivative claims and demand-futility arguments develop.

followups.question: What share reserve changes were made by the 2021 Equity Incentive Plan amendments approved on May 14, 2025 and May 13, 2026? Do any awards go to executives named in the class or derivative actions?
followups.rationale: Repeated plan amendments while insider-sale allegations are pending can attract stockholder scrutiny of compensation and dilution.

followups.question: What board process approved the $391M of FY2024 repurchases (3.81x net income), and did any named officers or directors sell shares while the company was buying back stock during the class periods?
followups.rationale: Buybacks above earnings that coincide with alleged misstatement periods and insider sales can be cited in derivative and securities claims.

followups.question: What controls ensure FEOC and domestic content compliance for the Section 45X credits sold: the $235.0M of 2025 AMPTC sold in March 2026 and up to $150.0M of 2026 AMPTC at 93% of face value? Do the sale agreements include indemnities or recapture obligations?
followups.rationale: A material liquidity source that depends on evolving Treasury guidance creates disclosure and contingent-liability exposure if compliance is challenged.

followups.question: With LFP battery cells sole-sourced from two vendors in China and new Section 301 tariffs of 10% to 12.5% announced July 23, 2026, what alternative sourcing or pricing actions are underway? How are these risks reflected in risk-factor disclosures?
followups.rationale: Concentrated supply and changing tariffs can cause margin shocks that, if under-disclosed, become the basis for securities claims.

followups.question: How are credit-loss allowances being set given management's statement on bankruptcies and closures among distributors and installers? What receivable concentration exists with financially stressed channel partners beyond the customer that caused the $6.2M FY2025 write-off?
followups.rationale: Under-reserved receivables in a distressed channel could lead to unexpected write-offs and questions about the adequacy of financial reporting.

followups.question: How were the $632.5M 0.0% convertible notes due 2026 settled, and what is the plan for the $575.0M 0.0% notes due 2028, including exposure under their fundamental-change repurchase provisions?
followups.rationale: Settlement mechanics and the remaining convertible obligation shape refinancing risk and potential bondholder claims in a change-of-control or distress scenario.

followups.question: What drove free cash flow down from $480M in FY2024 to $96M in FY2025 and to $26M in Q2 2026? How much of the increase in cash to $529M at Q2 2026 came from AMPTC sales and tariff refunds rather than operations?
followups.rationale: Dependence on one-time or policy-linked cash inflows reduces the cushion available for litigation costs and continued demand weakness.

followups.question: What explains the 29% decline in international revenue in Q2 2026? What channel inventory levels and sell-through trends is management seeing in those markets?
followups.rationale: Channel inventory build-ups or undisclosed regional weakness are common triggers for guidance misses and follow-on disclosure claims.

followups.question: With a current ratio of 3.45x and working capital of $1.39B at Q2 2026, what are the board's capital allocation priorities, including any resumption of buybacks halted since FY2025 Q3 and reserves for litigation?
followups.rationale: Capital allocation choices made during pending securities and derivative litigation are subject to board-level fiduciary scrutiny.
